title: Fillet wire
tagline: Round the corners of a wire or edge chain: an exact tangent arc Onshape recognises as an arc, or a smooth curvature blend -- picked corner by corner.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Onshape can fillet corners in a sketch, but not the corners of a wire. Fillet wire rounds chosen corners of any wire or edge chain -- in 2D or 3D -- and edits a wire body in place, so the untouched parts keep their identity.
useWhen: A wire (not a sketch) needs rounded corners
The fillets must be true arcs with a radius
A 3D corner needs a smooth (G2) blend
slides.caption: W1: two 90 deg corners filleted r10 (magenta).

points.head: Tangent
points.body: An exact arc, set back d = r tan(turn / 2), emitted as a sketch arc. Needs the corner to be planar.

points.head: Curvature
points.body: A G2 blend matching both edges' curvature, sized so its average curvature is 1/r. Works in 3D.

points.head: In place
points.body: A wire is split at the tangent points and only the corner pieces are replaced.

slides.title: The dialog
params: TANGENT: exact arcs. CURVATURE: G2 blends.
Off: only the corners you pick.
Filled by clicking corner points in the view; each can have its own radius.
Wire input: rejoin the pieces into one body.

slides.title: Examples
slides.head: W3: a line running into an arc, r10 -- the fillet is an exact circle tangent to both
slides.body: W1: two 90 deg corners, r10 -> one wire 291.416 mm long (300 - 4r + pi r). W4: a 3D corner with Tangent is skipped (not planar); W5: the same corner with Curvature -> a G2 blend, average curvature 0.1 /mm.

messages: With the reason: radius too large, no circle touches both edges, not in one plane (use Curvature), edges too short, or fillets overlapping.

items.head: Radius shown in Onshape
items.body: Tangent fillets are sketch arcs, so clicking one shows its radius.

items.head: No end keys yet
items.body: Fillet wire does not publish start / end keys.
